en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ucchaṅgapupphiya Bhaddāli-vagga, Chapter 7 [The Elder] who offered a flower from his lap, Having performed that deed with a pure mind, For eighty-four thousand aeons, I was reborn in the heavenly world. When the Blessed One appeared as a Buddha, Known by the name Padumuttara, I was reborn in the human world, Possessing great wealth and prosperity. I was well-versed in the Vedas, A master of the three branches of knowledge; I was honored by the king, And I lived in a village near the city. At that time, the Teacher, the Great Sage, Was wandering through the land of Magadha. Hearing of the arrival of the Buddha, I went out to meet him with joy. Seeing the Teacher, the Great Sage, With a heart full of serene faith, I took a flower from my lap And offered it to the Blessed One. Because of that offering of a flower, My body became fragrant and beautiful; I was reborn in the heavenly world, Possessing a divine form. Seeing the Teacher, the Great Sage, With a heart full of serene faith, I took a flower from my lap And offered it to the Blessed One. Because of that offering of a flower, My body became fragrant and beautiful; I was reborn in the heavenly world, Possessing a divine form. Through the ripening of that karma, I have attained this state of peace; I have reached the end of suffering, And I dwell in the bliss of Nibbāna. Thus did I offer a flower from my lap, And because of that, I have attained this state; I have reached the end of suffering, And I dwell in the bliss of Nibbāna. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Ucchaṅgapupphiya, The seventh in the Bhaddāli-vagga.
“At that time, in the city of Bandhumatī, I was a florist;
having filled my lap [with flowers],”
He entered the market town.
At that time, the Blessed One was seated in the midst of the community of monks.
With great majesty,
the Leader of the World departs.
Having seen the Lamp of the World,
To Vipassī, the savior of the world,
I took a flower from my lap and offered it to the Supreme Buddha.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I offered that flower in worship,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
my defilements have been incinerated... [and so on].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [and so forth].
The Buddha’s teaching has been proclaimed:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Ucchaṅgapupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Ucchaṅgapupphiya.
